analysis: The failure occurs during the 'after each' teardown hook when removing a temp workspace directory on a Windows runner, not during the test's actual assertions. EBUSY/resource-busy-or-locked errors on Windows rmdir typically indicate a lingering process (e.g., VS Code extension host, child debug process, antivirus, or file indexer) still holding an open handle on a file in the directory at deletion time. The PR under test (#19555) only modifies Aspire.Hosting.Radius backend/publishing code and its own unit tests, none of which touch the VS Code extension or its E2E fixtures/harness. This exact error signature (same fixtures.js:217:15 location, same EBUSY rmdir pattern) has recurred 20+ times across unrelated PRs, confirming it is a known environmental/timing flake in the Windows E2E test harness teardown rather than a code issue introduced by this PR.
